sections.shortTitle: Sindh Transfusion of Safe Blood Act 1997
sections.description:
Short title, extent and commencement

SINDH TRANSFUSION OF SAFE BLOOD ACT, 1997
SINDH TRANSFUSION OF SAFE
BLOOD ACT, 1997
An Act to regulate transfusion of
Safe Blood and Blood Products
[Gazette of Sindh, Extraordinary,
Part IV, 25th July, 1997]
No.PAS/Legis‑B‑15/96,
dated 25‑7‑1997.‑‑The Sindh Transfusion of Safe Blood
Act, 1997 having been passed by the Provincial Assembly of Sindh on the 5th
September, 1996 and assented to by the Governor of Sindh on 2nd July, 1997 is
hereby published as an Act of the Legislature of Sindh.
1. Short title, extent and
commencement.‑‑(1) This Act may be called the Sindh Transfusion
of Safe Blood Act, 1996.
(2) It shall extend to the whole
of the Province of Sindh.
(3) It shall come into force at
once.

dated 25‑7‑1997.‑‑The Sindh Transfusion of Safe Blood
Act, 1997 having been passed by the Provincial Assembly of Sindh on the 5th
September, 1996 and assented to by the Governor of Sindh on 2nd July, 1997 is
hereby published as an Act of the Legislature of Sindh.
2. Definitions.‑‑In
this Act, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context:‑‑
(a) "Authority" means
the Provincial Blood Transfusion Authority established under section 5;
(b) "blood bank"
includes all organisations carrying out all or any of the purposes of
receiving, preserving, storing analysing screening, processing and issuing
blood and blood products whether maintained by Government or private sector;
(c) "Government" means
the Government of Sindh;
(d) "prescribed" means
prescribed by rules made under this Act;
(e) "safe blood" means
human blood which is healthy and free from human Immunodeficiency (HIV),
Hepatitis B and C viruses or infective agents, like malarial parasites and
trepenema pallidum (syphilis) or such other viruses or infective agents as
Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify.

3. Transfusion of safe blood.‑Every physician,
surgeon, medical practitioner or any other qualified person transfusing blood
or blood product to any patient shall, before such transfusion, ensure in the
prescribed manner that the blood or as the case may be blood product, is
healthy and free from any virus or infection specified in clause (e) of section
2

4. Registration of blood
banks.‑‑(1) No blood bank shall receive or supply blood unless
it is registered with the Authority and holds a licence issued to it by the
Authority on payment of such fee as may be prescribed.
(2) No blood bank shall be
registered unless it conforms to the prescribed conditions of registration.

Function of the Authority

SINDH TRANSFUSION OF SAFE BLOOD ACT, 1997
SINDH TRANSFUSION OF SAFE
BLOOD ACT, 1997
An Act to regulate transfusion of
Safe Blood and Blood Products
[Gazette of Sindh, Extraordinary,
Part IV, 25th July, 1997]
No.PAS/Legis‑B‑15/96,
dated 25‑7‑1997.‑‑The Sindh Transfusion of Safe Blood
Act, 1997 having been passed by the Provincial Assembly of Sindh on the 5th
September, 1996 and assented to by the Governor of Sindh on 2nd July, 1997 is
hereby published as an Act of the Legislature of Sindh.
6. Function of the Authority.‑‑The
functions of the Authority shall be:‑‑
(a) to adopt/develop uniform
policy covering all aspects of safe blood transfusion based on current
developments in the field;
(b) to register and issue
licences to blood banks in the prescribed manner;
(c) to fix service charges of the
blood and blood products;
(d) to ensure that prescribed bio‑safety
measures and the instructions issued by the World Health Organization in this
behalf are strictly adhered to by the blood banks;
(e) to ensure that the blood
banks are managed and run by qualified professionals having posts graduate
qualifications in blood transfusion, hematology or clinical pathology
recognised by the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council;
(f) to monitor the working of the
blood banks and carry out periodical inspection;
(g) to perform any other
functions related to the matters aforesaid.

sections.shortTitle: Sindh Transfusion of Safe Blood Act 1997
sections.description:
Responsibilities of blood banks

SINDH TRANSFUSION OF SAFE BLOOD ACT, 1997
SINDH TRANSFUSION OF SAFE
BLOOD ACT, 1997
An Act to regulate transfusion of
Safe Blood and Blood Products
[Gazette of Sindh, Extraordinary,
Part IV, 25th July, 1997]
No.PAS/Legis‑B‑15/96,
dated 25‑7‑1997.‑‑The Sindh Transfusion of Safe Blood
Act, 1997 having been passed by the Provincial Assembly of Sindh on the 5th
September, 1996 and assented to by the Governor of Sindh on 2nd July, 1997 is
hereby published as an Act of the Legislature of Sindh.
7. Responsibilities of blood
banks.‑‑Every blood bank shall‑‑
(a) have a separate department,
staff and equipments for the purpose of blood donations and for selection,
handling care and safety of the donors;
(b) select donors of blood in
accordance with the instructions issued by the Authority;
(c) cause the donated blood and
blood products to be screened, examined and tested in accordance with the World
Health Organization's instructions issued for detection of any communicable
disease;
(d) possess equipment required
for haemoglobin estimation, blood grouping, cross matching, anti‑bodies
detection and screening of infective agents, such as human immunodeficiency,
hepatitis viruses, malaria and syphilis;
(e) equip itself with proper
refrigeration of blood and blood products and make arrangements for uninterrupted
power supply for refrigeration;
(f) observe standard operation
procedures approved by the Authority and more particularly as may be
prescribed;
(g) prohibit acceptance of blood
from processional blood donors; and
(h) submit periodical reports in respect
of detection of anti‑bodies and screening of infective agents.

8. Provincial Blood
Transfusion Committee.‑‑Government may, for the purpose of
creating awareness for availability of safe blood and motivation for voluntary
blood donations, set up a Provincial Blood Transfusion Committee consisting of
philanthropists, social workers and other such persons as ii may deem appropriate.

9. Penalty for contravention.‑Any
person contravening the provisions of this Act shall be punishable with
imprisonment which may extend to two years, or with fine up to five hundred
thousand rupees, or with both.

Court shall take cognizance of any contravention under this Act, except on a
complaint in writing made by the Chairman of the Authority or a person
authorized by him.
